packageManager: nuget (PackageReference; no Node toolchain in this repo)
node: n/a — this repo has no Node build step

distribution.windows: single-file portable exe (self-contained + needs-dotnet10 variants); a portable build does not self-update, the app's opt-in update check downloads the new build and tells the user where it landed

updater: in-app, opt-in, default off — the only network path this program has; it downloads the release zip, verifies it against the published SHA256SUMS.txt, and unpacks it next to the running copy without replacing it

signing.windows: unsigned; the SmartScreen warning is documented in the README and in the release body

versionSource: git tag vX.Y.Z, injected with -p:Version by the release workflow; the csproj falls back to `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` for local builds and to VersionFallback when that fails
release: single job: publish both profiles -> SHA256SUMS (LF) -> provenance attestation -> publish + make_latest -> assert releases/latest points at the tag; the job runs under the `release` environment (no required reviewers — see deviations)
actionPins: major tags (@v7); exact version (@v7.0.1) when tighter is needed; never full SHA

deviations.reason: Windows-only by construction: window placement goes through Win32 SetWindowPos/SetWindowPlacement, the global mouse hook is WH_MOUSE_LL, and elevated-window handling is UIPI. A macOS/Linux build would be a different program, not a port.
deviations.revisitWhen: only if a Windows-on-Linux/Wine distribution becomes a stated goal

deviations.reason: No code-signing certificate yet. The release body and the README both tell the user to click 'More info -> Run anyway', which is the documented interim state rather than an oversight.
The update check IS built in, but it is off by default: this program must not contact the network unless the user asks it to. Ticking the box is the only thing that ever goes online.
deviations.revisitWhen: first user request to default it on, or 2027-01-01

deviations.reason: The `release` environment exists so the publish step is recorded as a deployment, but it has no required reviewers — a pushed tag still publishes immediately. The maintainer decided against a human gate for now.
deviations.revisitWhen: the first time a bad release has to be forward-fixed, or when the repo gains outside contributors

notes: audit.mjs reads `platforms` and `deviations[]` only. rule == 'platforms' narrows the platform matrix; rule == <finding id> (e.g. windows-unsigned) moves that finding to 'accepted' (not counted in P0/P1/P2). A deviation without reason + revisitWhen is reported as drift. `updater-default-off` and `release-approval` are not finding ids — they are recorded here so the next reviewer does not have to rediscover them. Everything else is guidance for the agent.
